the analysis of the mechanisms underlying PDs induced by ILS in the motor area of the photosensitive baboons.

the sink in layer III, which is the earliest and most intense, could be of dendritic origin and the sink in layer V could result from passive effects due to active sources located in layer III or VI.
ILS PDs are triggered by a visual input, probably of cortico-cortico nature, which reaches the motor area and provokes a synaptic activation of the dendrites of the pyramidal neurons.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

ILS triggered discharges are generated by the superficial layers of area 4, which are activated by cortico-cortico projections, and that the wave corresponds to a synaptic inhibition in the deeper layers.

the visual cortex of baboon, in contrast to that of human, does not seem to be the site where the PDs are triggered, since the earliest and the most prominent sink of the PD is detected in the motor cortex.
ILS triggered epileptiform discharges are generated by a complex interaction of visual and somatic afferents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CSD analysis is a useful tool in studying the mechanisms of epileptic discharges induced in photosensitive baboon by intermittent light stimulation.

the CSD method applied to the study on the epileptic discharges induced in the photosensitive baboon by ILS, allows us to localize the main synaptic and dendritic events which occur in the motor and the premotor areas.
CSD can be used to investigate the mechanisms underlying epileptic discharges in a model of human epilepsy, and that the results obtained by this method are consistent with those of other studies.
